james: Heads-up — running nightly throughput sweep hit a surprising regression on llama-2-13b when RoPE scaling is enabled (scale=0.125). Throughput drops ~28% for batch>=12. Repro: `./bench --model llama-2-13b --ctx 4096 --batch 16 --rope-scale 0.125`

maria: ugh, saw something like this earlier with mixtral but couldn't reproduce. do you have perf profile?

james: pasted the hotpath from perf-runner: 
```
hot kernels:
  attention_forward: 42.1% (kernel selected: fused_attn_v2)
  matmul: 31.0% (aten_gemm)
  kv_cache_write: 12.4%
  kv_cache_eviction: 6.2%
  other: 8.3%
config: batch=16 ctx=4096 rope_scale=0.125 quant=fp16
observed: kernel_choice_switch at seq=512 -> fused_attn_v2 falls back to aten_gemm for later heads
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.58 -> drops to 0.36 after eviction burst
```

ben: interesting that kernel selection flips. could be because sequence length distribution changes internal heuristics (fused_attn becomes suboptimal after RoPE alters head dim rounding).

sara: @james can you attach the microtrace? also did you run with continuous batching on/off? that changes effective sequence packing.

james: attached trace snippet (short): `trace://1782004521/james/1` — we ran with continuous batching=on and max_batch=32. With continuous batching=off the regression is smaller (~12%).

tom: my hunch: RoPE scale changes the effective per-head FLOP pattern which nudges kernel_selector thresholds. If fused kernel expects certain stride/padding it might fall back to a slower path when head_dim%8 != 0 after quantization rounding.

lucy: can we bisect kernel_selector thresholds quickly? we should check the decision function: `select_attention_kernel(head_dim, seq, device)` — maybe a strict cutoff on seq*head_dim.

ben: quick experiment: pinned `select_attention_kernel` to always prefer fused_attn_v2 for this model and re-ran bench. Throughput recovered to near-baseline but latency P99 regressed a bit for small batches. So it's a tradeoff.

maria: that suggests fused kernel is faster for bulk throughput but has higher variance for small requests. For hosted tier we might prefer stable P99, but dedicated customers expect throughput.

james: profiling also shows KV cache eviction spike correlates with kernel flip. When fused kernel used, KV writes are coalesced better; fallback path triggers many small writes -> eviction thrash. That explains hit rate drop.

perf-bot: regression alert: job=throughput-sweep/llama-2-13b/178200 shows delta -27.8% vs baseline (178120), flagged for infra-eng review.

sara: next actions: 1) run targeted bisect on selection cutoff (seq*head_dim threshold) 2) try continuous batching tweaks to avoid pathological packings 3) test with KV cache padding heuristics (pad to nearest 64)

tom: I'll run the bisect today. quick patch outline: toggle `ATTN_FUSED_THRESHOLD` in runtime conf and run bench for values [2e3, 5e3, 1e4, 2e4]. script: 
```
for t in 2000 5000 10000 20000; do 
  RUNTIME_CONF=\"ATTN_FUSED_THRESHOLD=$t\" ./bench --model llama-2-13b --ctx 4096 --batch 16 --rope-scale 0.125
done
```

lucy: also add a heuristic to avoid tiny KV writes: when fallback path chosen, buffer writes and flush every N tokens or when buffer>8k. Should reduce eviction churn.

james: noted. i'll spin up a dedicated run that toggles buffer flush vs immediate write. If that fixes hit_rate we can keep kernel_selector as-is and patch cache behavior.

ben: one more thought — RoPE scaling sometimes changes per-head norm distribution; maybe we should include a quick quant-aware head_dim rounding step in model loader that picks quantization block sizes to preserve alignment. That would prevent kernel flip due to rounding differences.

maria: agree. action owners: tom=bisect kernel threshold, lucy=proto buffer flush, james=kv hit-rate runs and attach microtraces, ben=model-loader alignment idea POC. I'll consolidate results in the perf tracker ticket.

james: thanks all. ping me if you need the bench artifacts. I'll update with numbers later today. :thumbsup:
